question: Many urban areas that have developed close to rivers remain exposed to hydrogeological risk, and this has been compounded by periods of exceptional rainfall due to climate change coupled with the erosion of riverbanks by flash floods.

One of the goals of the Biodiversity Strategy for the near future is to restore both freshwater ecosystems affected by pollution and hydromorphological changes, and 25 000 km of the EU’s watercourses. Municipalities located in floodplain or estuary areas are very often unable to bear the huge financial costs of the environment regeneration needed to resolve the problems posed by hydrogeological risk.

In light of the above, can the Commission state whether it will allocate, not least in view of the goals of the Biodiversity Strategy, amounts that enable municipalities located on floodplains to take regeneration measures aimed at ensuring their hydrogeological safety?
answer: EU support to increase hydrogeological safety and resilience, including through nature-based solutions, is available to complement national and sub-national funding. Cohesion Policy (1) financing for investments in climate adaptation and disaster risk prevention for 2021-2027 amount to EUR 14 billion.

This will reduce the vulnerability to flood risk of more than 40 million people through investment in protection infrastructure, including green infrastructure (e.g. restoring floodplains). Another EUR 24 billion will support sustainable, integrated urban strategies, with special attention to environmental and climate challenges. Projects related to environmental regeneration can be supported.

Cohesion Policy is ran under shared management. This means that programmes are managed by Member States, who decide, within the objectives of the programmes, on the launch of calls and the projects that will be financed under each call.

The European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development may provide support for restoration of rivers, wetlands, peatlands, the restoration and management of floodplains in agricultural land following natural disasters and adverse climatic events and preventive actions, if such interventions are programmed in the Common Agriculture Policy Strategic plan for the area (2).

Recovery and resilience plans allocate approximately EUR 4 billion in estimated costs to support flood protection measures under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (3). Support is also available under the LIFE programme and the EU Mission on Adaptation, for example on climate risk assessments or adaptation measures.
All funding opportunities can be found in the guide ‘Find your EU Funding Programme for the Environment’ (4).

Regulation (EU) 2021/1060 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 June 2021 laying down common provisions on the European Regional Development Fund, the European Social Fund Plus, the Cohesion Fund, the Just Transition Fund and the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund and financial rules for those and for the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund, the Internal Security Fund and the Instrument for Financial Support for Border Management and Visa Policy, OJ L 231, 30.
